node.title: Re: system() call mis-directs?
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Then inside the script we fork off ... We then waitpid inside the forked process

This sounds a lot like what [doc://system] already does. Why do this twice?

we have found that in some cases the upgrade.pl child process starts out writing to its parent process log (do-upgrades.log), and in other instances it writes to worklog correctly as directed

Obviously, if you could narrow this down in which cases this happens (as others have pointed out, e.g. for what values of $sensor) more and make it more reproducible, that would be the best thing.

system("./upgrade.pl $sensor >> worklog 2>&1")

This kind of thing may work when $sensor is tightly controlled (see my node [id://1180578|here]!) and the system it is being run on never changes ([id://1205217]), but I would still strongly recommend against it. Also, what is the first line of upgrade.pl? If it's #!/usr/bin/env perl, its execution is dependent on PATH. Anyway, if upgrade.pl is a short-lived process, then I'd recommend [mod://IPC::Run3] instead; if it is a longer process that needs to run in the background while your script continues, then [mod://IPC::Run]. Both of these modules allow to avoid the shell and can still redirect STDOUT and STDERR.
